newsitem.title: JAPAN: Israel mandates Nomura as lead manager for samurai.
newsitem.headline: Israel mandates Nomura as lead manager for samurai.

text.p: Israel has awarded the mandate to lead manage its debut samurai bond to Nomura Securities, a senior Israeli Treasury official said here on Tuesday.
Treasury Director-General David Brodet said the issue will be between 15 to 20 billion yen and is intended to set a benchmark for Israeli sovereign borrowing.

The syndicate will include Yamaichi Securities, Nikko Securities, Daiwa Securities, Morgan Stanley, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan and Kokusai Securities as co-managers, he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
The issue is expected to be launched in late May or June, he said.
"This is not only to set a benchmark for Israel, it's also to make Israel known in the financial markets," Brodet said.
Brodet said the Treasury would discuss marketing the samurai issue to both retail and institutional investors in Japan.

He said no decision has been made yet on whether the debt issue will be a straight samurai bond or whether it might include some kind of structure to offer an enhanced yield to Japanese investors. But he said that issue would be taken up with the syndicate "in the next few days".
The proceeds from the samurai offering will be kept in yen, Brodet said.
"From the yen, we don't need to swap to dollars," he said.
Israel has already made offerings in the Yankee and Eurobond markets and plans to raise another $200 million in Yankee bonds later this year.
Israel is preparing for the expiry of the U.S. loan-guarantee programme through which it has borrowed $7.35 billion since 1992. That program expires in October 1998.

Brodet said the samurai issuance would make it easier for Israel to tap into the Japanese investor base for funds in coming years, either through issuing another samurai bond, or potentially as part of a global offering.
